studies.finding: Behavioural activation for depression: scheduling activity before motivation returns reduces symptoms, restoring exposure and mastery as active ingredients.

studies.name: Keltner & Lerner 2010
studies.finding: Experiments found fear raised and anger lowered perceived risk, showing that specific emotions steer judgment beyond the objective facts.

studies.name: Anderson & Kilduff 2009
studies.finding: In unacquainted groups, dominant members gained influence because they visibly signalled competence, and observers could detect those cues.

studies.name: Argyle & Dean 1965
studies.finding: Gaze-equilibrium model: people tune eye contact to keep total intimacy comfortable, so too much or too little gaze triggers compensatory looking away.

studies.name: Kwallek et al. 1991
studies.finding: Office-colour experiments: wall colour shifted workers' mood and error rates, with men more distracted in a red office and women in a green one.

studies.name: Henderson & Cote 1988
studies.finding: Logo-design study of 195 logos: distinctive, natural, harmonious designs elicited stronger affect and better recognition, the basis of standard branding guidelines.

studies.name: Rissanen & McQuillan 2016
studies.finding: Zero Waste Fashion Design: worked methods and exercises for cutting garments so textile waste is eliminated at the design stage.

studies.name: Otta et al. 2019
studies.finding: Studies of smile types found raters judged genuine felt smiles as more sincere and attractive than posed smiles.

studies.name: Lavie et al. 2009
studies.finding: Perceptual-load experiments: attention has limited capacity, so under high load irrelevant clutter goes unprocessed, while spare capacity lets distraction in.

studies.name: Vazire 2019
studies.finding: Experience-sampling study testing whether people know their own momentary personality states, extending self-knowledge research beyond broad traits.

studies.name: Herz 2016
studies.finding: Review of odour-evoked memory: smells uniquely trigger vivid, emotional autobiographical memories and can influence mood and well-being.

studies.name: Osborne-Crowley 2019
studies.finding: Brain-injury study: recognizing others' emotions depended on the viewer's own subjective emotional experience rather than on facial expressivity.

studies.name: Elliot & Niesta 2008
studies.finding: Controlled experiments: red clothing and backgrounds increased men's attraction ratings of women, without changing perceived likability or competence.

studies.name: Pennebaker & Seagal 1999
studies.finding: Expressive-writing study: health benefits tracked how coherently writers formed their story across sessions, with more coherent narratives linked to fewer doctor visits.

studies.name: Gottman 1994
studies.finding: What Predicts Divorce: observational studies of couples showed criticism, contempt, defensiveness, and stonewalling predict marital breakdown.

studies.name: Borkovec 1994
studies.finding: Theorized that worry functions as verbal-linguistic avoidance that suppresses emotional processing, the account behind worry-postponement techniques.

studies.name: Gottman 2014
studies.finding: Principia Amoris: book-length summary of decades of couple research, with criticism and contempt as top predictors of breakup and repair attempts as the antidote.

studies.name: Porges 2011
studies.finding: Polyvagal theory: the ventral vagal system supports calm social engagement, and a warm prosodic voice and facial cues can signal safety to others.

studies.name: Craske 2014
studies.finding: Inhibitory-learning account of exposure therapy: new safety learning works best when people approach feared situations early instead of waiting for readiness.

studies.name: Krasman 2018
studies.finding: Found that acting as the source of others' feedback requests added to supervisors' stress, a measurable cost of taking on extra demands.

studies.name: Miller 2019
studies.finding: Therapist-authored guide to drawing the line in your head, heart, and home, with practical boundary-setting language.

studies.name: Leach 2006
studies.finding: In Australian samples, guilt and anger about in-group advantage predicted willingness to take political action to reduce it.

studies.name: van de Ven, Zeelenberg & Pieters 2009
studies.finding: Distinguished benign envy, which motivates improving oneself, from malicious envy, which motivates harming the other.

studies.name: APA 2020
studies.finding: Stress in America 2020 survey: 78 percent of adults called the pandemic a significant source of stress, and the report declared a national mental health crisis.

studies.name: NAMI 2023
studies.finding: Crisis guidance: treat talk of self-harm as urgent, and use 24/7 crisis lines such as 988 for immediate professional support.

studies.name: Goffman 1959
studies.finding: The Presentation of Self in Everyday Life: interaction as performance, with front-stage impressions managed and back-stage behaviour hidden.

studies.name: Bales 1950
studies.finding: Interaction Process Analysis: small groups develop both a task leader and a social-emotional leader, rarely the same person.

studies.name: Deutsch 1973
studies.finding: The Resolution of Conflict: cooperation and competition are self-reinforcing norms, and attacking problems rather than persons keeps conflict constructive.

studies.name: Hatfield 1994
studies.finding: Emotional Contagion: emotions pass between people through mimicry and feedback, so moods converge within groups.

studies.name: Hall 1976
studies.finding: Beyond Culture: distinguished high-context and low-context communication, so the same directness reads differently across cultures.

studies.name: Bennett 1993
studies.finding: Developmental model of intercultural sensitivity: people move from defending their own norms as universal to adapting behaviour across cultures.

studies.name: Ferris et al. 2003
studies.finding: Standard account of personal reputation in organizations: reputations form from others' observations over time and shape influence and career outcomes.

studies.name: Nisbett 2017
studies.finding: Review with de Oliveira arguing that culture shapes how people think about thinking, so inference habits differ across societies.

studies.name: DiFonzo & Bordia 2000
studies.finding: Survey of top PR professionals: corporate rumors thrive on uncertainty and anxiety, and timely accurate communication is the standard response.

studies.name: Fehr & Gachter 2002
studies.finding: Public-goods experiments: people paid from their own earnings to punish free-riders even with nothing to gain, and this altruistic punishment sustained cooperation.

studies.name: WHO 2018
studies.finding: Global status report on alcohol and health: documents alcohol's contribution to injuries and disease worldwide, with risk falling as consumption falls.

studies.name: Dunbar 2017
studies.finding: Survey and diary work on social eating: meals shared with others demand time and coordination and are linked to stronger bonds and feelings of closeness.

studies.name: Rempel, Holmes & Zanna 1985
studies.finding: Traced how trust in close relationships builds in stages: predictability first, then dependability, then faith in the other's motives.

studies.name: Stein, Walker & Forde 1996
studies.finding: Community survey found public-speaking fear was the most common social fear and often severe enough to affect work and treatment-seeking.

readingOrder.text: Start with README, then learn the evidence labels so Strong, Moderate, and Myth mean something.
Work through MIND first: emotions and habits make every social rep easier.
Move to PEOPLE and run ACTION_PLAN weeks 1 to 5 while the social skills are fresh.
Add BODY & SIGNALS: sleep, training, and grooming give you energy for the reps.
Then POWER: negotiation and influence work better after listening and warmth.
Read SHADOW before you need it: manipulation defense and rules for hard situations.
Use BRAIN for study systems, then CULTURE in small daily doses for conversation range.
Finish ACTION_PLAN weeks 6 to 12, then use SOURCES to go deeper on what helped.
Use SCENARIOS and DATING one situation at a time; say the lines out loud before using them.
Run VOICE & SPEECH drills five minutes daily and record yourself once a week.
Fix fit and grooming first, then build a small palette from PRESENCE & STYLE.
Read SELF & RESILIENCE and SOCIAL AWARENESS before a hard week; practise one boundary and one room-reading rep.
